This first bail application has been filed by applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.143/2023 registered at Police Station Kotwali Ashoknagr district Ashoknagar (M.P.), for an offence punishable under section 363, 366A,

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per the case of prosecution, father of the prosecutrix reported to PS Kotwali Ashoknagar on 10.03.2023 that his daughter is missing since morning.
Some unknown person has allured and taken his daughter.
PS Kotwali Ashokngar registered FIR in Crime No.143/2023 for offence punishable under section 363 of IPC.

During search, the prosecutrix was recovered on 13.05.2023 Indar Khede vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69498975/
1 from the house of accused Mukesh at village Sirlai PS Bhikan Gaon, Distt. Khargaon.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In her statement under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C, the prosecutrix alleged that accused Dharmendra had allured her and taken to the house of Mukesh and sold her for an amount of Rs.1,20,000/-.
Mukesh committed rape on her on the pretext of marrying with her.
She got pregnant.
She revealed to Mukesh that Dharmendra is not related to her and she left her home without informing her parents.
Thereafter, Mukesh contacted her parents.
The Police recovered her from the house of Mukesh from village Sirlai.
The applicant is father of Mukesh.
He had an altercation with accused Dharmendra when Dharmendra attempted to take the prosecutrix from to his home.
On such allegations, offence under Sections 363, 366A, 376(2) (n), 506, 370(A), 376, 120B, 34 of IPC and 5,9 of the POCSO Act were registered.
The charge sheet has been filed on 18.07.2023.
The applicant was arrested on 17.07.2023 and he is in custody ever since.
Learned counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has falsely been implicated in the matter.
The applicant is aged 50 years and agriculturist by profession.
He has a family to look after.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no chance of his absconding leaving behind his family and property.
No case is made out against the applicant.
He is not involved in the alleged offence of abduction and rape.
Learned counsel submits that when the prosecutrix revealed about leaving her parental home without informing her parents, Mukesh himself contacted her parents.
This goes to show bonafide on the part of the applicant.
Learned counsel further contends that Co-accused Bhuriya Bai has been granted bail vide order dated 1st June, 2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.23465 of 2023.
The applicant's case is on better footing, therefore, he may also be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, but without commencing on merits of the case, this Court inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
